bloghow-to-teach-a-dachshund-to-heel.author: Michele Gabriella
bloghow-to-teach-a-dachshund-to-heel.text: Karen is an awesome trainer.  I bought two puppies from her and she inspired me to train them in obedience (see Sadie’s photo above). I am now working on my CDX with my 2nd doxie, Colby. I found that it’s really worth it to train my dogs. It’s a thrill to be successful at an obedience trial! Not only do my dogs love the attention and the training, but it also forges a strong bond between us.

bloghow-to-teach-a-dachshund-to-heel.author: Arleen
bloghow-to-teach-a-dachshund-to-heel.text:
This is a great article about obedience. I had to laugh when you said, “I can’t stress enough, be careful not to step on your dog!”  I have done that with my dog and it has taken her a long time to trust my big feet.

The one thing that I observed Karen, is that you are very upbeat with your dogs while training and in the ring. I don’t think that your dogs think it is work but having fun and wanting to please you.

By the way, should the color of your shoes and pants match the color of the dog in the ring?

bloghow-to-teach-a-dachshund-to-heel.author: Ed
bloghow-to-teach-a-dachshund-to-heel.text: This is a great article.  I know how hard you work at getting perfection in the ring with your doxies!

bloghow-to-teach-a-dachshund-to-heel.author: Hannelore Damrow
bloghow-to-teach-a-dachshund-to-heel.text:
I have very much enjoyed your obedience blog as we have CDs and CDX in the past; only 2 were with our Dachsies who have passed away from old age..

I found your methods very encouraging and am eager to try again with the passing of time. My daughter in WI does agility and showed me the touch system which she uses too.

Hopefully you will consider us future Harlequin owners. Sincerely, Hannelore Damrow

bloghow-to-teach-a-dachshund-to-heel.author: Karen
bloghow-to-teach-a-dachshund-to-heel.text: Hannelore – Thank you for your comments. I hope we can talk about training more! Please tell me more about the touch system in agility training, as I am unfamiliar with that. I would love for you to begin to train one of our puppies!

bloghow-to-teach-a-dachshund-to-heel.author: Stacy
bloghow-to-teach-a-dachshund-to-heel.text:
Hi Karen,

I just wanted to tell you how much I am enjoying your articles and your website. I was initially drawn here because of the beauty of your dogs, but more importantly their  versatility! I just lost my best friend last month and while I still have two senior dogs whom I love completely, the hole in my life is threatening to swallow me. He was special and there won’t be another to take his place. I cried for your Bailey because I understand that loss far too well. I actually have my dog’s half sister but she sadly is nothing like him, and at almost 15 with her fair share of health issues, I will feel her loss far too soon. I am glad that you had Cherry and Abby to find focus and hope. 

I am so impressed with your approach to these wonderful dogs and your obvious love. We are kindred spirits in our doggie approach. I have mad respect and admiration for you and what you are doing!

bloghow-to-teach-a-dachshund-to-heel.author: Margaret
bloghow-to-teach-a-dachshund-to-heel.text: It looks like it has been awhile since anyone has commented on this post, but it resonates with me even years after it was written.  My heart was completely stolen by a little dachshund we rescued when he was age 8 and loved until he death at age 19.   The rescue was my husband’s doing — he arrived home with him, and I did not want the dog.   But he was wonderful and soon wormed his way in to my heart so deeply that I have not been ready for another dachsie for 25 years.  He loved everyone, lived with a bunch of other dogs and got along with them all, raised two kids who were NOT in the picture when he showed up, sat up in the begging position so long he would fall asleep and fall over backwards.  He set the barre pretty high. This post reminds me that hearts do heal, and while the next generation cannot replace the last, there is hope for loads of fun ahead.

bloghow-to-teach-a-dachshund-to-heel.author: Adriana Woodward
bloghow-to-teach-a-dachshund-to-heel.text:
Love your writing! I can feel your passion for the pups and the training!

I am getting a pup soon since I learned to love the breed after my teenager boy begged for one 10 years ago!!

Our “Marley” is soooo smart and mischievous at times haha.

Thank you 😊

blogchoosing-and-training-a-dachshund-pu.author: John
blogchoosing-and-training-a-dachshund-pu.text: All these training tips are how my family and I raised our previous Dachshund, and were perfectly in line with how my girlfriend and I planned on training our puppy. This is all good information.

blogchoosing-and-training-a-dachshund-pu.author: Karen
blogchoosing-and-training-a-dachshund-pu.text: John – Thanks for your comment.  I hope you can apply these training tips when you get your new puppy home!

blogchoosing-and-training-a-dachshund-pu.author: Leslie Anne Chatfield
blogchoosing-and-training-a-dachshund-pu.text: These guides are right on point!  At their best, mini dachshund’s ‘focus and attitude’ are hard wired and guided into great performance by a fun-loving, clear, patient handler. And the dachshund independence part? Indeed! When the focus and attitude are working well together with a handler who has been clear about what is expected, ~ it’s really amazing! Worth every second of patience and practice ~ great doggy fun! I run in Iron Doggy events with my mini l/h alongside K-9 unit shepherds and malinois’ and she, with her little legs flying thru the air on a dead heat run, holds her own amazingly ~ she’s got the attitude, she loves the fun, the run, the challenge, and working as a tight pair! So focused! Impressive!  Hoping to represent the “Harlequin Dachshunds” line sometime in the not too distant future!

blogchoosing-and-training-a-dachshund-pu.author: Cindy Tesler
blogchoosing-and-training-a-dachshund-pu.text: I agree that not all puppies are born equal. You also said that a Dachshund’s natural instincts are to hunt and think independently. I think it’s a good idea to choose a breeder that allows you to come and see your puppy before they come home with you.

blogchoosing-and-training-a-dachshund-pu.author: Linda Cain
blogchoosing-and-training-a-dachshund-pu.text: This is such good information.. I lost my Yorker and miss her so..  I have been looking at miniatures dachshunds   They are beautiful dogs and I hope to purchase one.  I would like to know where you are located. I am from Indiana. Thank you. Linda Cain

blogchoosing-and-training-a-dachshund-pu.author: Karen
blogchoosing-and-training-a-dachshund-pu.text:
LInda, Thank you for your email.  We are located 20 minutes southeast of Philadelphia, PA.  Since you are from Indiana, I suggest that you try to locate an AKC “Breeder of Merit” closer geographically to you.  You might start by looking at websites for 
Dachshund Club of America
, and also National Miniature Dachshund Club 
National MIniature Dachshund Club
.  They list breeders by state, so you may be able to find a nice puppy locally.  Thank you for searching out reputable breeders and staying away from Pet Shops and puppy mills.  Karen

blogchoosing-and-training-a-dachshund-pu.author: Sandy
blogchoosing-and-training-a-dachshund-pu.text:
GREAT article! My husband and I are just starting to research miniature dachshunds, having only owned large breeds before. Your training tips are a bit different that what I did with my mastiffs, and if I should be so lucky to find a good mini doxie breeder that choses to place a pup with me, I will follow these tips!

By the way, your 2018 litter is gorgeous. I am heartbroken you are so far away!!  We are in CT and struggling to find a good mentor/breeder…alas. Thank you for such an informative and beautiful website.

blogchoosing-and-training-a-dachshund-pu.author: Shirlane and Mike Yannuzzi
blogchoosing-and-training-a-dachshund-pu.text: We were so lucky to adopt Joey from you 2018 litter.  He is a beautiful dog, his temperament is ideal and he is an awesome companion.  EVERYONE loves Joey!  Your tips were quite helpful to us as new dog parents.  Thank you so much.

blogchoosing-and-training-a-dachshund-pu.author: Pam
blogchoosing-and-training-a-dachshund-pu.text: , Thank you so very much for all your useful information. Although our Rusty is not a dachshund, you are an encyclopedia of knowledge. I intend to follow through with everything that I’m hearing from you to help train our sweet puppy.

blogdachshund-agility-training.author: Sheryl Ann Yamuder
blogdachshund-agility-training.text:
This is a great article, truly inspirational.  As someone who has always taken my dog everywhere, I can relate to the changes in a dogs personality when they go for rides, travel, spend time with other people and dogs and generally are well socialized.

I can’t ever imagine just keeping my dog at home.  I also think keeping a dog solely at home creates a viscous circle.  Many people say they do not take their dogs places because the dog does not like strangers, children or other dogs.  How could the dog like these interactions if they have never been exposed to them.  I have been thinking about doing training with my next dog and this article clearly shows that it is a worthwhile experience for both you and your dog, no matter how well the dog does.

Thank you for writing this,

Sheryl Ann

blogdachshund-agility-training.author: Karen
blogdachshund-agility-training.text: Thank you for your comments.  I truly hope that this article serves as a springboard for you to begin regularly training your dachshund puppy for agility or obedience.  She can be great!!

blogdachshund-agility-training.author: Kathy Corbett
blogdachshund-agility-training.text:
I enjoyed this article very much and congratulate Karen and Chelsea on their accomplishments. 

Karen and I train at the same facility so I have had the opportunity to watch her train several of her dogs. Patience, Perseverance and Success is evident in her training style. I admire the connection that Karen has with her dogs.

I, too, believe that the bond you make whilst training your dog is so very worth the time.

blogdachshund-agility-training.author: Karen
blogdachshund-agility-training.text: Thanks for your comments, Kathy.  As with dachshunds, your breed, the Sharpei, is not really known for performing obedience either.  Nevertheless, any breed can be successful if you are willing to work at it.  The secret is to know your breed (and what it takes), but especially know your dog.  Some take longer than others.  Often the ones that take the longest to reach your goal are the ones whom you are most proud of in the end. Go for the gold, and never let anyone tell you it can’t be done. Good luck training your dogs!

blogdachshund-agility-training.author: Debbie Gupton
blogdachshund-agility-training.text: Loved reading this inspirational story on a dedicated Dachshund owner/ breeder/ handler , her girl, and all their successes. It gave me an emotional boost to continue seeking out training methods to make my two babies , not just “couch pets” . We are very active and want to take our pups with us EVERYWHERE.  Thanks Karen

blogdachshund-agility-training.author: Sandra
blogdachshund-agility-training.text: This is an awesome account!!!!!! I love doxies.

blogdachshund-agility-training.author: Diane WAtson
blogdachshund-agility-training.text:

blogdachshund-agility-training.text: Hi Karen! Your blog about training Chelsea is great!  I’m a Bayshore Club member. Lost Devo in Nov; he was on wheels.  Working on CDX with my shepherd in barbara class.  When ready, I  would love one of your Dachshunds for obedience.  Love that Rock Star. Beth Johnson

blogreasons-not-to-buy-pet-store-puppies.author: Cathie
blogreasons-not-to-buy-pet-store-puppies.text: I agree Karen.  Also, people should know that breeders breed to improve the breed often times keeping multiple puppies for themselves to show, train and love. Breeders rarely profit from selling puppies. Puppy mills that supply puppies to the pet stores produce in mass quantities and do it strictly for profit. Their dogs are raised I filthy conditions much of the time.  Every puppy deserves a good home. It’s just not a good idea to support this type of reproducing.

blogreasons-not-to-buy-pet-store-puppies.author: Buddy
blogreasons-not-to-buy-pet-store-puppies.text: Great advice from a great breeder. Thanks for the information.

blogreasons-not-to-buy-pet-store-puppies.author: MGabby
blogreasons-not-to-buy-pet-store-puppies.text: Many people searching for a pet are not well informed as to the correct breed for their family or their lifestyle. Keep in mind that the purpose of the pet shop is to sell puppies quickly; not to ensure a good pet for the family.  The breeder will be most concerned about where the puppy is placed and that it is a good “fit.”    Hope everyone who reads this will heed your advice. Thank you Harlequin Dachshunds for great information as well as beautiful puppies!

blogreasons-not-to-buy-pet-store-puppies.author: Sharon Trombetta
blogreasons-not-to-buy-pet-store-puppies.text: Excellent Information!  We breeders work very hard to have the healthiest parents and pups in our programs.  The pups are our responsibility for their lifetime. Owners will benefit from the support and education that is available to them.  Many times I hear “well we bought our dog from a broker who gets them from reputable breeders.”  We do not sell our pups to brokers!  They are the puppy mills incognito. This information needs to get out to the general public.

blogreasons-not-to-buy-pet-store-puppies.author: Karen
blogreasons-not-to-buy-pet-store-puppies.text: I agree, Sharon. We need to get the word out that reputable breeders will NEVER place their puppies with brokers for pet shops. Only backyard breeders and puppy mills, often with dogs of inferior quality or poor health, will allow their puppies to be sold at a pet shop.

blogreasons-not-to-buy-pet-store-puppies.author: Regina l
blogreasons-not-to-buy-pet-store-puppies.text: I couldn’t even imagine purchasing a puppy from a pet store. I have two dachshunds, both from Harlequin Dachshunds. They have the most wonderful dispositions, very social with other dogs and just love children. Also they are beautiful dogs; I get stopped all the time with compliments!  Thank you Karen for bringing such joy into our lives with your very special puppies.

blogreasons-not-to-buy-pet-store-puppies.author: The Hendershot Family
blogreasons-not-to-buy-pet-store-puppies.text: My family purchased our sweet little Doxie, Scarlett, in 2006 from a pet store. While we wouldn’t have changed Scarlett for the world, we will NEVER buy from a pet store again. Scarlett’s back problems started at the age of two years. We just figured “she’s a Doxie” and it’s to be expected, we soon found she had an extra vertebrae. Off and on for years Scarlett would have flare ups and need to be on medications. In 2015, Scarlett was diagnosed with SARDS. It’s a condition that mimics Cushings Disease and causes blindness. Cushings can be treated, there is not treatment for SARDS. Scarlett went from being an energetic happy pup to a lazy OVERWEIGHT pup. She doubled her weight even though she at 3/4 cup of Science Diet weight control a day. Our vets were concerned but realized she just didn’t have it in her to play and run like before. They didn’t feel she was in pain and she was still a happy sweetie, just a true lap dog now. One of the worst days of our lives was October 18th. Scarlett went into cardiac arrest at the emergency vet. We lost our sweet angel. Words cannot describe how devastated we were and still are. We have spent THOUSANDS caring for our Scarlett. We have since learned that another dog from the same pet store and likely from the same litter passed away last year. We always heard Doxies lived long lives. Scarlett would have been 11 on November 5th. Our house feels empty without Scarlett.  My family is looking to bring a new female Doxie into the family this coming spring/summer. We are researching and speaking with AKC breeders and will NOT be purchasing from a pet store EVER AGAIN!

blogreasons-not-to-buy-pet-store-puppies.author: Karen
blogreasons-not-to-buy-pet-store-puppies.text: Thank you for sharing Scarlett’s story.  As the blog indicates, puppy mills are the primary source of puppies for pet stores.  They are out for a profit and are not concerned about the health and well-being of the dogs that they produce.  On the other hand, the breeders’ goal is to improve the quality of the breed as much as possible, by using only as parents only dogs who are healthy and have correct structure.  I often review 4 or 5 generations of pedigrees before deciding to breed any particular dog.  Of course there are no guarantees in life, but you would be much less likely to encounter genetic health problems by purchasing a puppy from a responsible breeder who is dedicated to the breed.

blogreasons-not-to-buy-pet-store-puppies.author: Lucinda McLaren
blogreasons-not-to-buy-pet-store-puppies.text: Thank you for featuring adult dogs on your website.  I’ve owned dogs since 1958 and know all too well how easy it is to fall in love with a puppy, not realizing that an adult dog is hiding inside.  For the past decade, I’ve taken in retired breeding animals and have loved my older dogs.  They are house broken and past the chewing stage.  They also appreciate a quiet life.  It is wonderful of you to promote the adult dog.

blogreasons-not-to-buy-pet-store-puppies.author: Stuart M. Kaplan
blogreasons-not-to-buy-pet-store-puppies.text:
We lost our little friend 3 months ago.  His name was Lucky, although he wasn’t very lucky health wise.  My daughter bought him from a pet shop, and from the start,  he was “touch and go” with a bad kennel cough.  He also had a rather nasty temperament. He came to live with us after he bit too many kids and my daughter was at her wits end. At 6 yrs of age he went blind from SARS he hung in there.  We found talking toys for him so we could still play.  Unfortunately both his kidneys failed last year and at 10 years of age the vet said he couldn’t survive this time so we had to euthanize my little buddy.

It took some time for us to accept his loss but we decided it’s time to bring a new doxie into our lives.  Lucky was a long haired miniature black with some tan coloring I was hoping to find a similar looking doxie.

I have no intentions of showing,  but would just like a new friend, but more importantly, a healthy dog from a reputable breeder, such as Harlequin Dachshunds.  Thank you for the opportunity to post my negative experience with a pet shop purchase. 

Looking forward to hearing from you.  Thanks

blogreasons-not-to-buy-pet-store-puppies.author: JANE BROWN
blogreasons-not-to-buy-pet-store-puppies.text: Wish more people could read this.  Maybe then they wouldnt buy from pet stores.

blogreasons-not-to-buy-pet-store-puppies.text:
